title: Inquest to probe death of woman in police cell
article: An inquest is scheduled to begin today into the death of a 42-year-old Prince George woman who died in police custody.
Cheryl Ann Bouey was arrested along with a companion near the College Heights pub for being intoxicated in a public place in June 2008 and held in detention.
Some time after she was put in a cell she was found unresponsive during a regular check. An ambulance was called, but attempts to revive her were unsuccessful.
The week-long coroner's inquest will be held at the Prince George Law Courts before coroner Rodrick MacKenzie and a jury.
The jury can make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths but not findings of legal responsibility.
There are three investigations into the death: an inquiry by the chair of the Commission for Public Complaints against the RCMP, the coroner's inquest, and an independent police investigation.
